| F2 | defect | MAJOR | HIGH — any daemon started with a scratch state dir silently repoints the operator's REAL global Claude config at a path that will be deleted, and reinstalls accumulate entries instead of reconciling them. The installed command is `&lt;state_dir&gt;/claude-session-start-pij.sh`, but the homes it is written into are always the real ones from `claude_homes()`. Nothing gates this: there is no flag, no env opt-out, and `--offline` does not cover it. The PM's own isolated proof is the demonstration — assets/live-auto-seat.md's spine row 1 is `config.claude-hook-ensured … {"after":"/tmp/pij-plan127-refresh-rs/claude-session-start-pij.sh","home":"/Users/jordanknight/.claude"}`: a temp-dir command written into the operator's real settings. The PM restored the file afterwards (I confirmed ~/.claude/settings.json has no SessionStart entry today and still has crossSessionInbound=accept), but the next person running a dev daemon gets no such discipline. The second half is that the stale entry is never reconciled: my probe shape `stale-pij-path` (an existing entry whose command is a DIFFERENT …/claude-session-start-pij.sh) plans a Write that APPENDS a second pij entry rather than updating the first. Both then run on every session start; the dead one is a `sh` command that cannot be found. This machine already has two state dirs in play (~/.pij-rs and ~/.pij-rs-dev), so this is reachable today, not hypothetical. Plan 126's inbound ensure was safe to run unconditionally because its value is a constant; this one is not, because its value depends on the daemon's state dir. Risk r2 is only half-mitigated: the path is stable per state dir, not stable per machine. | crates/cli/src/main.rs:954-961 | — | Smallest fix, in order of preference: (a) when an existing SessionStart entry's command already ends in `/claude-session-start-pij.sh`, REPLACE that entry's command rather than appending a new one — that makes reinstall converge and kills the accumulation; plus (b) skip the Claude-home ensure unless the resolved state dir is the default one, or honour an explicit `PIJ_RS_NO_CLAUDE_CONFIG=1`, so a scratch daemon cannot edit the operator's global config at all. (a) alone fixes the accumulation; (b) alone fixes the blast radius; the PM should say which it takes and why. | — | — | — | out-of-tree probe shape `stale-pij-path` → EnsurePlan::Write appending a second entry (existing entry preserved, len 1→2); assets/live-auto-seat.md spine row 1; crates/cli/src/main.rs:954-961 read for any guard (none) |
| F3 | defect | MINOR | MEDIUM — `pij doctor claude-hook` blames someone else's hook for pij's absence. When a home has a SessionStart hook that is not pij's, `plan_claude_session_start_hook` returns Write with `before = first_hook_command(...)`, i.e. the FIRST command in the array, which is simply a foreign hook. The doctor's status ladder then reads `report.command.is_some()` and prints `status: wrong-command`, `configured: /usr/local/bin/my-own-hook`. Nothing is wrong with that command and pij never configured it — the true state is `hook-missing`. A diagnostic that names an unrelated owner's config as the misconfiguration is worse than no diagnostic: the reader's next move is to go and change a hook that was correct. Verified by probe: `foreign-sessionstart-only` → installed=false, command=Some("/usr/local/bin/my-own-hook"); `hooks-but-no-sessionstart` and `no-hooks-at-all` → command=None (so the classification depends on unrelated content, not on pij's own state). The installed case is fine — the NoChange arm sets `before` to our own command, and `installed-plus-foreign-first` reports installed=true with the right command. | crates/cli/src/main.rs:928-940 | — | Smallest fix: in the Write arm of `plan_claude_session_start_hook`, return `before: None` (drop the `first_hook_command` call) so `wrong-command` fires only where it means something — or, better and still small, have inspect distinguish `stale pij command present` (an entry ending in `/claude-session-start-pij.sh` that is not the expected path — the F2 case, genuinely worth reporting) from `foreign hooks only`, which is `hook-missing`. | — | — | — | out-of-tree probe over `inspect_claude_session_start_hook`: no-hooks-at-all → command=None; foreign-sessionstart-only → command=Some("/usr/local/bin/my-own-hook"); hooks-but-no-sessionstart → command=None; stale-pij-path → command=Some("/old/pij/…"); installed-plus-foreign-first → installed=true |
| F4 | question | MINOR | MEDIUM — the reason given for the additionalContext payload is asserted, never tested, and it is the packet's own least-confident item. docs/how/claude-auto-seat.md states the hook 'emits only valid SessionStart JSON context so Claude refreshes its initial UI after the seat exists'. The live asset shows the statusline carrying the id ten seconds after a zero-input start — but that observation is equally consistent with the statusline simply re-rendering on its own throttle, because there is no run WITHOUT the payload to compare against. Both worlds have to emit a distinguishable artifact before the causal claim is earned. This matters beyond tidiness for two reasons. First, the payload is not free: it injects a sentence into the context of every session the hook fires for, and if the matcher `""` matches all SessionStart sources it fires on resume, clear and compact too, not only startup. Second, a correct rule resting on a wrong reason is a latent repeal — the next person who finds the refresh happens anyway will delete the payload, and if it was in fact load-bearing they will reintroduce the bug the payload was hiding. G1 asks for one line to a log; the line it gets carries no diagnosis. Keeping stdout empty on the failure path is what matters for the hook contract, and that is preserved either way. | — | — | — | out-of-tree shell probe, 7 environments under `env -i` with shimmed pij/pij-rs: both-ok → rc=0, only the SessionStart JSON on stdout; pij-rs-missing → skip:no-daemon; pij-missing and adopt-refuses → identical refused:adopt lines; adopt-noisy (adopt writes to stdout and stderr) → correctly suppressed, only the JSON emitted |
